title: How Much Money Do You Need to Start Amazon FBA?
content:
One of the most common questions beginners ask is: "Can I start Amazon FBA with no money?"

The honest answer is no. Because you are buying physical products to sell, you need some starting capital. However, you do not need to be rich to start.

Here is a realistic budget breakdown for a beginner starting a small private label brand.

1. Product Inventory ($500 - $1,000)

This is your biggest expense. You want to buy your first batch of products from a manufacturer (usually on a website like Alibaba).

  • The Goal: Start small by ordering 200 to 300 units of a lightweight, affordable item to test the market safely.

2. Samples and Shipping ($150 - $300)

Before buying hundreds of items, you must pay the supplier to mail a single prototype sample to your house. This ensures the quality is perfect. You will also pay shipping companies to move your bulk order from the factory directly to Amazon's warehouse.

3. Amazon Seller Account & Tools ($150)

  • Amazon Professional Account: Costs $39.99 a month to legally sell as a business.
  • Product Research Software: Tools like Helium 10 or Jungle Scout cost around $50 to $70 for your first month to help you track market data.

Total Realistic Starting Budget: $1,000 - $1,500

While some people try with less, having around $1,200 gives you a comfortable safety cushion to launch your first product successfully without running out of cash.
